title: Three companions
hookLine: Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala are killed in Delhi for refusing to give up their faith

cards: This is a hard day in the story, so it goes gently. After listening to the pandits, Guru Tegh Bahadur decided to go to Delhi himself, to stand for them before the emperor. He did not go alone.

A few close companions went with him, men who had served him for years. Tradition says they were arrested on the way and brought to Delhi in chains. The authorities wanted the Guru to give up his faith, and he would not.
So, tradition says, they tried to break him by making him watch what happened to his friends. Today, three names Sikhs say with love.

teach.b: Their names were Bhai Mati Das, his younger brother Bhai Sati Das, and Bhai Dayala. Bhai means brother, the title Sikhs give to respected members of the community.
Mati Das and Sati Das were brothers from a Brahmin family who served as the Guru's close aides and scribes. Dayala was a devoted companion from the same circle.
In Delhi, in November 1675, each of them was offered the same bargain: give up your faith and live. Each refused.

And each was put to death, tradition says in front of the Guru, in the old city, near where Gurdwara Sis Ganj stands today. Tradition remembers the manner of each death in painful detail, and Sikhs recall it every year.
Here, only this much: they were killed with great cruelty, and they did not bend. What Sikhs hold onto is how they faced it.

Tradition says Bhai Mati Das was reciting the Japji, Guru Nanak's morning prayer, which you met near the start of this path, and kept reciting to the end. Tradition says each of the three stayed calm, and kept the Name.
None of them was a Guru.

They were ordinary members of the community, a scribe, his brother, a friend, and they are remembered today in the Ardas, the prayer Sikhs say together, among those who gave their lives rather than give up their faith.
The Sikh story honors not only its Gurus, but the companions who stood beside them.

how: Sikhs remember Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala among the martyrs recalled in the Ardas, and a museum and memorials near Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Delhi honor them.

o: three pandits who traveled from Kashmir for help
the first three Sikhs to become Gurus after Nanak
the Guru's friends who would not give up their faith

p: recited the Japji to the end

s: none of them was a Guru. they were ordinary members of the community.
they were offered their lives if they gave up their faith

games.q: you're Bhai Mati Das, in Delhi, told to give up your faith or die. what do you do?
o: refuse, and keep reciting the Japji.
ask the Guru to decide for you.
games.why: tradition says he refused and kept reciting Guru Nanak's Japji to the end. his brother and Bhai Dayala refused too.

practice: If you have a candle or a small lamp, light it; if not, just picture one, and watch the flame.
Let the three names move slowly through your mind, Mati Das, Sati Das, Dayala, then widen your thoughts to anyone, anywhere, who has suffered for holding to what they believe.
You don't need words; just keep the flame company, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Three companions. Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala, the Guru's friends, killed in Delhi in 1675 for refusing to give up their faith.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi: brother, the title of respect given to devoted Sikhs.

carryVoice: Your line: they did not bend. A scribe, his brother and a friend, remembered in prayer to this day. Seventy-eight days now.

sources.ref: Sikh tradition on the martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala, Delhi, November 1675
